page: Amazon Web Services c5.9xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processors running at a base clock frequency of 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources comprise 18 physical cores yielding 36 virtual CPUs with two threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA, which accelerate floating-point arithmetic and cryptographic computations.

The server is provisioned with 72.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring persistent workloads to attach remote network block storage. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, while GPU hardware acceleration is absent with zero installed graphics processors.

Benchmark assessments place the c5.9xlarge consistently in the mid-range performance tier across standard enterprise evaluations. The server logged a multi-core score of 33,337.29 on stress-ng and 10,571.0 on Geekbench multi-core, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 30,341.37. Uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth measurements registered 104.53 GB/sec read and 45.25 GB/sec write. In transaction and throughput profiling, the platform delivered 30.97 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 19.51 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure and resource efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high compute density relative to its memory footprint. Without onboard NVMe storage, the architecture incurs an operational tradeoff by relying strictly on remote storage volumes for input and output operations. The instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration build clusters, distributed scientific modeling, Clang software compilation pipelines, and CPU-bound web service deployments.
